model_annotation: Figure 3(a) displays a line plot illustrating the coverage metric as a function of the number of completions (k), for four distinct Llama baseline models. The x-axis, labeled “Number of completions (k)”, is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 2^10 to 2^27, with tick marks at intervals of 2^10, 2^12, 2^14, 2^16, 2^18, 2^20, 2^22, 2^24, 2^26, and 2^28. The y-axis, labeled “Coverage”, ranges from 0.0 to 0.8. The plot includes four lines, each corresponding to a different model: “Llama-3B” (blue solid line with circle markers), “Llama-3B + FT” (green dashed line with triangle markers), “Llama-1B” (orange dash-dotted line with square markers), and “Llama-1B + FT” (red dotted line with diamond markers). All four lines show a similar trend, starting at approximately 0.4 coverage at k=2^10, rising to a peak near 0.65 coverage at k=2^20, and then gradually declining to approximately 0.55 coverage at k=2^28.
